problem_restatement.problem: The open SPCX short uses a venue mark-price stop, but the prior three-second public mark recorder was not running when the current v51 lifecycle entered.
problem_restatement.success_criterion: Capture future SP500 and SPCX mark observations at a three-second target cadence without constructing any execution client or changing v51 behavior.
problem_restatement.non_goal: The recovered recorder cannot retroactively fill any historical mark gap or prove that an unobserved mark did not cross the stop.

current_spcx_lifecycle.interpretation: No retained mark observation crossed the stop, but the historical 110.796-second gap prevents a proof that no brief crossing occurred.

hypothesis_ledger.hypothesis: REST supplementation will keep prospective SP500 and SPCX lifecycle mark gaps within five seconds when the update-driven WebSocket stream becomes sparse.
hypothesis_ledger.minimum_update_evidence: One complete eligible lifecycle whose merged mark path has no gap above five seconds.
falsifiers: any merged lifecycle mark gap above 5000ms
stale recorder status during an open lifecycle
a venue mark crossing the stop without the expected protected close

recommendation.Recommendation: Keep v51 unchanged and use the recovered recorder only as prospective evidence for the open and future index lifecycles.
recommendation.Why now: SPCX is open near its fixed stop and its trade-candle high cannot establish whether the venue mark trigger fired.
recommendation.Evidence reviewed: Current v51 SPCX ledger, 63,810 retained WebSocket mark samples, current venue protection, prior capture journal, recorder implementation, and focused tests.
recommendation.Observed problem or opportunity: The current lifecycle is protected, but exact stop-path attribution is weaker than the configured five-second research contract.
recommendation.Applicable market regime: All source-native SP500 and SPCX v3 lifecycles because the same venue mark-price stop semantics apply.
recommendation.Alternatives considered: Infer from trade candles, relax the gap rule, manually intervene, or restore unsigned mark capture; only the final option preserves execution and evidence integrity.
recommendation.Expected upside: Future stop and drawdown diagnoses can use exact mark-source evidence instead of a mismatched trade-price proxy.
recommendation.Main risks and failure modes: The recorder may stop or be rate-limited, and it cannot repair pre-recovery evidence gaps.
recommendation.Validation completed: No-order contract, authority-none status, bounded real heartbeat, exact symbol binding, and focused unit tests.
recommendation.Validation still required: Continuous merged-path gap audit through a fully resolved source-native lifecycle.
recommendation.Success metrics: No gap above five seconds across a resolved lifecycle and exact reconciliation between mark trigger, venue stop, and close fill.
recommendation.Failure / rollback triggers: Recorder heartbeat becomes stale, any identity/schema mismatch occurs, or merged path evidence exceeds the five-second limit.
recommendation.Confidence level: High on recorder isolation and current venue protection; medium on prospective path completeness until a full lifecycle resolves; low on SPCX strategy expectancy at the current sample size.

limitations: The current lifecycle began before recorder recovery and remains technically unresolved under the strict five-second path contract.
Periodic REST samples are local-receipt observations rather than exchange-timestamped mark events.
No strategy, route, asset, parameter, sizing, leverage, stop, exit, execution behavior, or deployment configuration changed.
